# HoundShield — AI Compliance Firewall

> HoundShield is a local-only AI compliance firewall for defense contractors,
> healthcare organizations, and law firms. It intercepts AI prompts before they
> leave the customer's network, scans them for CUI, PHI, PII and secrets on the
> customer's own hardware, and produces tamper-evident evidence mapped to
> NIST 800-171 and HIPAA.

## What HoundShield does

Employees at regulated organizations paste sensitive data into ChatGPT, Copilot,
Claude and Gemini. That creates a compliance exposure — CMMC Level 2, HIPAA,
SOC 2 — because the data travels to a third party outside the organization's
control.

HoundShield is an OpenAI-compatible proxy. The customer changes one base URL:
instead of pointing AI tools at api.openai.com, they point them at their own
HoundShield endpoint. Every prompt is scanned locally. Prompts containing CUI,
PHI or PII are blocked and written to a SHA-256 hash-chained audit log. Clean
prompts pass through unchanged.

## Deployment modes — this distinction matters

- **Mode A — hosted trial.** Runs on Vercel, which is NOT FedRAMP-authorized.
  For demos and non-CUI, non-PHI evaluation only.
- **Mode B — self-hosted Docker.** Runs on the customer's own infrastructure.
  This is the CUI-safe mode: prompt content never leaves the customer boundary.
- **Mode C — air-gapped.** Isolated network. CUI-safe. For IL-5+ environments.

The "data never leaves your network" property is true of Modes B and C. It is
NOT true of the hosted trial. Do not describe the hosted endpoint as CUI-safe.

## Who it is for

- Healthcare privacy officers and CISOs at 50–300 person physician groups and
  clinics protecting PHI under HIPAA
- IT security managers and ISSOs at 50–500 person DoD subcontractors preparing
  for CMMC Level 2
- IT directors at law firms protecting privileged communications
- RPOs, MSPs and compliance consultancies delivering assessments to those clients

## Pricing — one offer

**CMMC AI Risk Assessment Report — $499, one time.** The proxy runs for 14 days
in the customer's own environment; they receive a SHA-256-signed PDF that
risk-scores every AI prompt event against NIST 800-171 Rev 2 and HIPAA, plus a
30-minute readout. No subscription, no per-seat licence, no MSA, no signup.
30-day money-back guarantee, honored after delivery.

RPO and MSP partners co-brand the same report at **$399** — a flat $100
discount off retail, not a revenue share — and set their own retail price.

There is no subscription tier. The in-browser scanner at /demo is free and
requires no account.

## Verified product facts

- **16 detection engines, 53 shipped regex patterns** covering CUI markings,
  CAGE codes, DoD contract numbers, clearance and ITAR terms, all 18 HIPAA
  Safe Harbor identifiers, PII, API keys and cloud credentials, source code
  and internal network data. Counts are computed from the shipped registry.
- **Scan latency p99 under 1 ms** (0.648 ms measured over 2,000 cold scans
  against a 10 ms budget). The benchmark runs in CI and can be reproduced by
  anyone from the repository.
- **All 110 NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 controls** mapped, with SPRS scoring.
- **SHA-256 hash-chained audit log**, append-only and tamper-evident.
- Detection patterns are plain regex in an MIT-licensed public repository, so a
  buyer can read and verify them before purchasing.

## What HoundShield does not claim

- No SOC 2 report today. A SOC 2 Type I audit is planned, not complete.
- No FedRAMP authorization. The hosted plane runs on Vercel.
- No ISO 27001 certification. Control mapping only.
- No published customer count, and no customer logos.

## Regulatory context (current as of 2026-08-19)

CMMC Phase 2 enforcement was suspended by the Department of War on 13 July 2026
pending a Reform Task Force review. Phase 2 was not cancelled and the
10 November 2026 date has not been replaced. DFARS 252.204-7012, all 110
NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 controls, and the annual SPRS self-assessment remain in
force. DOJ's Civil Cyber-Fraud Initiative has settled 15 False Claims Act cases
over inflated self-attestations.

ChatGPT is not HIPAA-compliant without a Business Associate Agreement; OpenAI
offers a BAA only for its API and enterprise products.

## Partner program

The partner channel is **RPOs, MSPs, MSSPs and compliance consultancies**.
Assessment organizations (C3PAOs) are not eligible: conflict-of-interest rules
bar an assessor from recommending products to organizations it assesses. The
report is designed to be handed *to* an assessor as evidence; the assessor
stays independent.

## Competitor comparisons

Written from publicly available information, with review dates on each page.
HoundShield does not publish competitor contract prices.

- vs Nightfall AI: https://www.houndshield.com/compare/nightfall
- vs Prompt Security (SentinelOne): https://www.houndshield.com/compare/prompt-security
- vs Microsoft Purview + GCC High: https://www.houndshield.com/compare/microsoft-purview-gcc-high
- vs Polymer: https://www.houndshield.com/compare/polymer
- vs Strac: https://www.houndshield.com/compare/strac
- vs WitnessAI: https://www.houndshield.com/compare/witnessai

The honest summary: most AI DLP tools inspect prompts in the vendor's cloud,
which is the transfer a regulated buyer is trying to avoid. Prompt Security
shipped an on-premises option in 2026, so local deployment is no longer unique
— but it arrives as an enterprise SKU through enterprise procurement. What
HoundShield offers that the others do not is a $499 one-time, control-mapped
evidence deliverable a small organization can buy without a procurement cycle.

## Technical

- Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, Docker
- Compatible with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini,
  Copilot, open-source models)
- Audit format: SHA-256 hash chain, append-only, PDF export
- Integration: one base-URL change, no per-machine agent
